packet_framing_waveform.tlp_framing: STP (K27.7) → 12-bit Sequence Number → TLP header (3 or 4 DW) → optional data payload → 16-bit LCRC → END (K29.7), or EDB (K30.7) for nullified TLP.
packet_framing_waveform.dllp_framing: SDP (K28.2) → DLLP type byte + DLLP-specific fields → 16-bit CRC → END (K29.7).
packet_framing_waveform.lane_placement: STP / SDP MUST be placed on Lane 0 when the Link is wider than x1.
packet_framing_waveform.logical_idle: When no TLP / DLLP / ordered-set is being transmitted, IDL data character (00h) is sent on all Lanes, scrambled and 8b/10b-encoded.

TS1.purpose: Polling / Configuration / Equalization training; carries Link Number, Lane Number, N_FTS, the Data Rate Identifier (incl. 32.0 GT/s bit), EQ presets/coefficients, and Alternate Protocol Negotiation fields.

TS2.purpose: Final-handshake training set confirming Lane/Link and rate/EQ agreement before sustaining the trained rate.

SKP.purpose: Skip ordered set; clock-tolerance compensation (±300 ppm) and carrier for Lane Margining control.

FTS.purpose: Fast Training Sequence — exit L0s to L0.

EIOS.purpose: Electrical Idle Ordered Set before TX enters Electrical Idle.

EIEOS.purpose: Electrical Idle Exit Ordered Set — re-acquire block lock on exit.

ltssm_transition_trigger_waveform.Polling_to_Configuration: Sufficient consecutive TS1/TS2 ordered sets with valid Lane/Link numbers observed.
ltssm_transition_trigger_waveform.Configuration_to_L0: Lane width + Lane number agreement complete; initial L0 at 2.5 GT/s for backward compatibility.
ltssm_transition_trigger_waveform.L0_to_Recovery_for_speed_change: Either end initiates a data-rate change; TS1/TS2 advertise the target rate via the Data Rate Identifier.
ltssm_transition_trigger_waveform.Recovery_Equalization_at_32GTs: If both ends advertise 32.0 GT/s, Recovery runs the Phase 0-3 enhanced equalization (with preset hints and retimers) before settling at 32 GT/s.
ltssm_transition_trigger_waveform.L0_to_L0s: TX sends EIOS then enters Electrical Idle (per direction).
ltssm_transition_trigger_waveform.L0_to_L1: Both ends agree via PM DLLPs; transitions through Recovery.

clock_tolerance_compensation.purpose: SKP ordered sets let the receive elastic buffer absorb/generate symbols to compensate up to ±300 ppm clock-rate mismatch; at Gen5 SKP also carries Lane Margining control.

general_timing_rule: PCI Express 5.0 is character-timed at a 31.25 ps Unit Interval per Lane (32 GT/s, NRZ). Higher-level state machines (LTSSM sub-states, Recovery.Equalization, FC init, Replay) are specified in Symbol/Block Times so they scale across generations.
transmitter_eye_diagram_reference: Figure 4-32 — Minimum Transmitter Timing and Voltage Output Compliance Specification.
receiver_eye_diagram_reference: Figure 4-34 — Minimum Receiver Eye Timing and Voltage Compliance Specification.

voltage_levels.modulation: NRZ (two-level); eye opened by transmitter four-phase EQ + receiver CTLE/DFE.
voltage_levels.lane_margining: Receiver eye margin measured in-system via time (left/right) and optional voltage (up/down) margining.

line_rate_waveform.encoding: 128b/130b — 128 payload bits + 2-bit sync header per 130-bit block; ~1.54% overhead.

block_framing_waveform.block_layout: 2-bit sync header (10b = Data Block, 01b = Ordered Set Block) + 128-bit scrambled payload, per lane.
block_framing_waveform.tlp_framing: TLP bytes carried inside Data Blocks; framing tokens are byte values, not 8b/10b K-codes.
block_framing_waveform.lane_placement: First byte of any TLP/DLLP on Lane 0 when wider than x1.

equalization_waveform.description: At 32 GT/s the link runs Recovery.Equalization through four phases, exchanging transmitter coefficient/preset requests between partners and through any retimers, until the eye is open.
